title: enterprise-onboarding-and-support-playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook

Overview
This playbook documents Redwood Inference’s standardized process for onboarding enterprise customers and operating ongoing support, including integration guidance, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, routine health checks, and QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), SRE, and Product Liaisons supporting enterprise accounts.

Goals
- Accelerate time-to-value for enterprise customers while reducing operational risk.
- Provide a consistent, auditable onboarding checklist and technical integration path.
- Ensure clear escalation and incident resolution flows with SLAs and ownership.
- Supply repeatable QBR and health-check artifacts for renewal and expansion conversations.

Scope
Applies to all enterprise customers (annual committed spend or Dedicated/Private deployments). Excludes small self-serve customers and community pilot accounts.

Owner and Contributors
- Playbook owner: Maya Chen (Customer Success)
- Technical owner: Lead Solutions Engineer (eng-developer-experience)
- Operational partner: SRE (eng-sre)
- Reviewers: see metadata

Onboarding Phases (high-level)
1. Discovery (pre-contract)
   - Outputs: Security questionnaire answers, high-level architecture, integration constraints, target SLOs, success criteria.
   - Owners: CSM (commercial), SE (technical).
2. Kickoff (week 0)
   - 60–90 minute kickoff meeting with stakeholders: CSM, SE, SRE lead, customer technical leads, security.
   - Deliverables: Project plan, contact matrix, network/IP allowlist, data flows, and timelines.
3. Integration (week 1–4)
   - Implement API keys/credentials, VPC peering or Private deployment setup, test prompts/evals, and telemetry ingestion.
   - SE runs integration checklist.
4. Validation (week 2–6)
   - Functional validation (end-to-end), load validation (if Dedicated), and quality validation (prompt set regressions).
   - Run acceptance tests: latency, throughput, example prompt outputs, fallback behavior.
5. Handover to Support & Ops (post-acceptance)
   - Finalize runbooks, escalation contacts, and schedule first QBR.

Detailed Technical Integration Checklist
(Use this as a gating checklist — every item should be marked Done/Blocked/NA in the customer project plan.)
- Customer account and billing setup completed.
- Provision API keys: note key ID prefixes and owner aliases.
- Networking
  - For hosted customers: record customer IP ranges and configure allowlist.
  - For Dedicated/Private: validate VPC peering, route tables, and NAT/GW settings.
  - Confirm 443 egress to api.redwood-inference.internal (for private control plane, use customer-specific endpoint).
- Authentication & Secrets
  - KMS/HSM integration verified (if required).
  - Rotation policy documented.
- Data handling
  - Confirm data residency settings and retention policy.
  - Document PII redaction or tokenization requirements.
- Model & Config
  - Target model(s) selected and pinned (version).
  - Quantization/latency profile set for Dedicated instances.
  - Batching and cache settings recommended by SE.
- Telemetry & Alerts
  - Logging set up to customer SIEM (if requested).
  - Metrics ingestion to Redwood Console: latency-percentiles, token-rate, error-rate, model-fallbacks.
  - Create initial dashboards and alert policies.
- Tests
  - Functional: sample prompt set (10–50 prompts) passed.
  - Load: spike test up to agreed baseline RPS and sustained test for throughput.

SLOs and Monitoring Recommendations
- Platform SLOs we commit to during onboarding conversations:
  - Uptime (control plane & inference endpoints): 99.9% monthly (Dedicated SLA variations discussed per contract).
  - Latency: 95th percentile request latency <= 250 ms for standard generation paths; 95th percentile <= 500 ms for long-sequence or reranking workloads.
  - Error rate (5xx + client error retries): < 0.5% target in steady state.
- Alert thresholds (suggested initial settings):
  - High latency: p95 > 400 ms for 5m window (page SRE).
  - Increased error rate: >1% for 5m window (page SRE).
  - Throughput saturation: CPU/GPU queue > 70% for 10m (notify capacity team).

Escalation Playbook (condensed)
Purpose: Provide a predictable path for fast resolution of customer-impacting issues.
- Level 0 — Customer Success (CSM/SE)
  - Ownership: First touch, triage communications, runbook checklist.
  - When: Billing questions, minor config issues, documentation clarifications.
  - Channels: ##cs-{customer-shortname} Slack, csm-enterprise@redwood.internal alias.
- Level 1 — SRE / Oncall Engineer
  - Ownership: Operational incidents impacting availability or latency within SLOs.
  - When: Elevated alert firing (latency, error rate), request queues growing, degraded throughput.
  - Pager: SRE oncall (rota via PagerDuty: team "redwood-sre") and #incident channel.
  - Action: Execute runbook, collect logs (request IDs, spans), escalate to Level 2 if unresolved after 30 minutes.
- Level 2 — Serve/Runtime & SEs
  - Ownership: Deep diagnosis (model runtime, kernel failures, memory/cuda OOM), mitigation (fallback to alternate model/config).
  - When: Persistent errors after Level 1 runbook, unknown error patterns, perf regressions.
  - Contacts: Lead runtime engineer, assigned SE.
  - Action: Apply mitigation (route to model-variant, scale up Dedicated capacity), coordinate customer communication cadence.
- Level 3 — Engineering/Product Leadership
  - Ownership: Code-level fixes, cross-team change coordination, contractual impact assessment.
  - When: Customer outage > 4 hours, data integrity or security incidents, major regression.
  - Action: Assemble war room, exec updates, post-incident review.

Escalation Communication Templates
- Initial acknowledgement (CSM): "We’ve received your report and are triaging. Next update in 30 minutes. Points of contact: <CSM name>, <SE name>."
- Incident update (SRE): provide timeline, impacted endpoints, mitigations applied, ETA for next update.

Known Issues and Workarounds (selection)
| Issue | Symptom | Root cause (if known) | Workaround / Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokenizer divergence on customer prompts | Slightly different tokenization leads to unexpected outputs | Non‑standard whitespace / invisible characters in upstream data | Normalize inputs (NFKC, strip zero-width chars). SEs should provide a normalize_preprocessor example. |
| Intermittent 502 errors during model rollover | 502s observed for ~1–5s during automated model swap | Short race when cache warm-up overlaps model switch | Retry with exponential backoff (100ms -> 1s). Schedule model rollovers during low traffic windows. |
| Increased p95 latency for long-context workloads | p95 spikes beyond expected when sequence length > 8k | KV cache eviction policies or insufficient batch window | Use pinned longer-context instance/enable KV cache persistence. If Dedicated, increase memory or apply quantization profile for long-context. |

Support Process & SLA Expectations
1. Customer reports issue via support portal or created Jira ticket (preferred for trackability).
2. CSM acknowledges within 1 business hour.
3. If severity == Sev1 (service down/major production impact), page SRE immediately.
4. Triage and mitigation steps documented in ticket.
5. Post-incident: owner prepares a postmortem within 3 business days (for Sev1) and schedules a 1:1 incident review with customer if requested.

Health Checks and QBR Materials
- Weekly health check (recommended during first 90 days)
  - Metrics: success-rate, p50/p95 latency, token consumption, model-fallback counts, cache hit rates, error trends.
  - Actions: surface anomalies, recommend config changes (batching, cache TTL).
- Monthly health check (post-90 days)
  - Same metrics; include cost-per-1000-token breakdown and unit economics.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) agenda template
  1. Attendees & objectives (5 min)
  2. Business outcomes & success metrics (10 min)
  3. Usage and cost summary (10 min)
  4. Performance & reliability (10 min)
  5. Security & compliance updates (5 min)
  6. Roadmap & product ask review (10 min)
  7. Action items & next steps (5–10 min)

QBR Deliverables (examples)
- Executive summary one-pager (health, usage, top risks, recommendations)
- Technical appendix (detailed metrics dashboard snapshots and raw CSVs)
- Action item tracker (owner, due date, status)

Handover Checklist (to Support/Operations)
- Documented runbook for the customer (location & access rights).
- Completed security & compliance artifacts (SOC/ISO evidence where applicable).
- Alerting on-call rules configured and validated.
- Escalation contacts verified and slack/jira access granted.
- Final acceptance sign-off from customer (email or signed doc).
